chunks: Ibn Abi al-Bilād narrated from his father, who attributed it to the Messenger of Allah (ṣ) that he said:

The Messenger of Allah (ṣ) said: 'Shall I not guide you to the best of moral traits of this world and the Hereafter?' They said, 'Yes, O Messenger of Allah.' He said: 'Whoever establishes ties with the one who cuts him off, gives to the one who deprives him, and forgives the one who wrongs him. And whoever would be pleased to have his life asked for (extended) and his sustenance increased, then let him be mindful of Allah and keep ties with his near relatives.'
ai.seo_question: What are the best moral traits for success in this world and the Hereafter according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith, found in *Kitab al-Zuhd*, elevates *silat al-rahim* (maintaining kinship ties) from a social duty to a supreme spiritual practice that guarantees divine expansion of life and sustenance. It emphasizes proactive generosity—giving to those who withhold and forgiving those who wrong you—as the key to securing blessings in both the dunya and the akhirah. The narration concludes by linking these ethical behaviors directly to *taqwa* (God-consciousness), reinforcing the Shia emphasis on family bonds as a means of spiritual purification.
